title: Microsoft's 18 Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
description: Research-based guidelines for designing AI systems that work effectively with humans. Based on empirical research from Microsoft Research analyzing 150+ AI guidelines and validated through user studies. These guidelines address transparency, explainability, trust, fairness, and control in AI interactions.
published: CHI 2019: ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

guidelines.guideline_name: Make clear what the system can do
guidelines.description: Help users understand what the AI system is capable of doing. Set appropriate expectations by clearly communicating the scope, limitations, and intended use cases of the AI system.
guidelines.intent: Prevents user frustration and misuse by ensuring users understand the AI's capabilities and boundaries from the start. Clear capability communication helps users know when to trust the system and when to seek alternatives.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially those with limited or specialized capabilities

questions: Does the system clearly state what it can and cannot do?
Are the AI's capabilities communicated before the user starts interacting?
Are limitations and boundaries explicitly mentioned?
Can users understand the intended use cases?
Is the scope of functionality clear without trial and error?
what_to_look_for: Clear documentation of what the AI can assist with
Examples of tasks the AI can handle

best_practices: Provide concrete examples of tasks the AI can perform
Show capability demonstrations during onboarding
Display limitations prominently, not hidden in fine print
Use simple language to describe capabilities, not marketing jargon
Offer interactive tutorials that showcase main features
Update capability descriptions when the AI improves
Be honest about what the AI cannot do
Show the range of inputs the AI can process

common_issues.issue: Vague or overly broad capability claims
common_issues.example: AI assistant claims to 'help with anything' without specifying actual capabilities
common_issues.impact: Users develop unrealistic expectations and become frustrated when the AI cannot help

common_issues.example: Chatbot only works with English but this isn't mentioned until user tries another language
common_issues.impact: Users waste time attempting unsupported tasks

common_issues.example: AI tool launched without showing what kinds of problems it solves
common_issues.impact: Users must guess how to use the system effectively

guidelines.guideline_name: Make clear how well the system can do what it can do
guidelines.description: Communicate the AI system's expected performance level and accuracy. Help users understand not just what the system can do, but how reliably it can do it.
guidelines.intent: Enables users to calibrate their trust appropriately. Users need to know whether they can depend on the AI's outputs or should verify them independently.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, critical for systems making predictions or recommendations

questions: Is the AI's accuracy or performance level communicated?
Do users understand the reliability of the system's outputs?
Are confidence levels or uncertainty indicated?
Is performance communicated in user-understandable terms?
Are there metrics or benchmarks shared with users?

best_practices: Share accuracy metrics in user-friendly terms (e.g., '9 out of 10 times')
Show confidence levels for individual predictions
Provide examples of when the system performs well vs. poorly
Update performance claims as the system improves
Be transparent about known weaknesses
Use visual indicators for confidence levels
Compare performance to human benchmarks when relevant
Explain what factors affect accuracy

common_issues.example: Medical diagnosis AI doesn't share how often it's correct
common_issues.impact: Users cannot judge whether to trust the AI's recommendations

common_issues.example: Translation tool presents all translations as perfect without indicating uncertainty
common_issues.impact: Users may not verify outputs that contain errors

common_issues.example: Showing '87.3% F1 score' to non-technical users
common_issues.impact: Users cannot understand what the performance numbers mean

guidelines.description: Initiate AI interactions at contextually appropriate times. The system should appear when users need it, not randomly or at disruptive moments.
guidelines.intent: Prevents interruption fatigue and ensures AI assistance is perceived as helpful rather than intrusive. Well-timed interventions increase acceptance and usage.
guidelines.applicability: Proactive AI systems, notifications, recommendations, interruption-based interfaces

questions: Does the AI appear at appropriate times?
Are interruptions based on user context and state?
Can users control when the AI engages?
Does the timing respect user workflow?
Are urgent vs. non-urgent interventions appropriately timed?
what_to_look_for: Timing based on user activity patterns
Detection of appropriate moments to assist

best_practices: Detect moments of user uncertainty or struggle before offering help
Avoid interrupting during focused work periods
Allow users to set 'do not disturb' preferences
Queue non-urgent suggestions for natural break points
Use progressive disclosure - start subtle, escalate if needed
Learn user patterns to optimize timing
Provide immediate help for urgent situations
Defer optional suggestions to convenient moments

common_issues.example: AI assistant pops up tips while user is in middle of typing important email
common_issues.impact: Disrupts flow, reduces productivity, creates annoyance

common_issues.example: AI suggestions cannot be snoozed or dismissed permanently
common_issues.impact: Users feel lack of control, may disable AI features entirely

common_issues.example: Security alerts and promotional tips both interrupt with equal urgency
common_issues.impact: Users learn to ignore all notifications, missing important ones

guidelines.description: Display information that is specifically relevant to the user's current context, task, and goals. Filter and prioritize AI outputs based on what matters now.
guidelines.intent: Reduces cognitive load by showing only pertinent information. Users can focus on their task without being overwhelmed by irrelevant AI outputs.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially recommendation engines, search, and assistive systems

questions: Is displayed information relevant to the user's current task?
Does the AI filter out irrelevant results?
Is information prioritized by contextual importance?
Does the system adapt to user's current goals?
Are outputs tailored to the specific situation?

best_practices: Personalize outputs based on user context and history
Filter results by current task or project
Show location-aware or time-aware information
Prioritize by relevance, not just recency or popularity
Adapt to the user's expertise level
Consider device context (mobile vs. desktop)
Surface relevant information proactively
Hide or deprioritize irrelevant options

common_issues.example: AI recommendations ignore user's current project or role
common_issues.impact: Users must manually filter through irrelevant information

common_issues.example: Search results don't consider user's location when it's clearly relevant
common_issues.impact: Poor user experience, reduced trust in AI usefulness

common_issues.example: AI shows all possible options without prioritizing by relevance
common_issues.impact: Users are overwhelmed and may miss important information

guidelines.description: Ensure the AI system's behavior aligns with appropriate social and cultural norms for the context. The system should behave in socially acceptable ways.
guidelines.intent: Builds user comfort and trust by making AI interactions feel natural and appropriate. Violations of social norms can make users uncomfortable or reject the system.
guidelines.applicability: Conversational AI, social robots, customer service bots, any user-facing AI

questions: Does the AI communicate in socially appropriate ways?
Are cultural norms respected?
Is the tone appropriate for the context?
Does the AI respect social boundaries?
Are formality levels appropriate?
what_to_look_for: Professional vs. casual communication as needed

best_practices: Match communication style to the context (formal for business, casual for entertainment)
Respect cultural differences in different regions
Use appropriate pronouns and inclusive language
Avoid overly familiar or presumptuous behavior
Respect privacy norms (don't ask inappropriate questions)
Adapt to professional vs. personal contexts
Follow domain-specific etiquette (medical, legal, educational)
Allow users to set formality preferences

common_issues.example: Professional AI assistant uses overly casual slang in business context
common_issues.impact: Users perceive the AI as unprofessional or disrespectful

common_issues.example: AI uses idioms or references that don't translate culturally
common_issues.impact: Alienates users from different cultural backgrounds

common_issues.example: AI asks personal questions without establishing appropriate rapport
common_issues.impact: Users feel uncomfortable and may abandon the system

guidelines.description: Actively work to prevent and reduce social biases in AI outputs. Ensure the system doesn't perpetuate or amplify harmful stereotypes or unfair treatment.
guidelines.intent: Promotes fairness and prevents harm. Biased AI systems can perpetuate discrimination and cause real-world harm to marginalized groups.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, critical for systems affecting people's opportunities or treatment

questions: Has the system been tested for bias across demographic groups?
Are outputs fair and equitable?
Does the system avoid stereotypes?
Is there regular bias monitoring?
Are mitigation strategies in place?

best_practices: Test AI performance across diverse demographic groups
Use diverse and representative training data
Implement fairness constraints in model training
Monitor outputs for biased patterns
Conduct regular bias audits
Establish fairness metrics and thresholds
Include diverse perspectives in design and testing
Provide channels for reporting bias
Document known limitations and biases
Continuously improve based on bias findings

common_issues.example: Image generation AI consistently depicts doctors as male and nurses as female
common_issues.impact: Reinforces harmful stereotypes and limits representation

common_issues.example: Facial recognition works well for some skin tones but poorly for others
common_issues.impact: Creates unfair experiences and excludes certain users

common_issues.example: Hiring AI trained on historical data that reflects past discrimination
common_issues.impact: Perpetuates discriminatory practices

guidelines.description: Make it easy for users to invoke or activate the AI system when they need it. Reduce friction in accessing AI assistance.
guidelines.intent: Ensures users can quickly access AI help when needed. If invocation is difficult, users may not use the AI even when it would be helpful.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially optional or on-demand AI features

questions: Can users easily activate the AI when needed?
Are there multiple ways to invoke assistance?
Is invocation quick and low-effort?
Are invocation methods discoverable?
Can power users use shortcuts?

best_practices: Provide visible, easily accessible buttons or controls
Support keyboard shortcuts for power users
Enable voice activation where appropriate
Make AI features discoverable in context
Reduce steps required to invoke AI
Offer persistent access points (floating button, menu item)
Support gesture-based invocation on touch devices
Allow customization of invocation methods
Surface AI features at point of need

common_issues.example: AI assistant buried three menus deep in settings
common_issues.impact: Users don't discover or use available AI help

common_issues.example: Requiring multiple steps or specific sequences to activate AI
common_issues.impact: Users avoid using AI due to high friction

common_issues.example: AI only accessible via voice, no visual alternative
common_issues.impact: Excludes users in quiet environments or with speech difficulties

guidelines.description: Make it easy for users to dismiss or ignore AI outputs when they are not useful. Users should be able to quickly move on from unhelpful AI interactions.
guidelines.intent: Prevents AI from becoming an obstacle. Users need to maintain control and not be forced to engage with AI outputs they don't want.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially proactive and recommendation systems

questions: Can users easily dismiss AI suggestions or outputs?
Is dismissal quick and obvious?
Does dismissal stop the AI from repeating the same suggestion?
Can users opt out of AI features?
Are there no penalties for dismissing AI help?
what_to_look_for: No forced engagement with AI outputs

best_practices: Provide obvious close or dismiss buttons
Support ESC key and standard dismissal gestures
Remember when users dismiss suggestions (don't repeat)
Allow permanent dismissal of recurring suggestions
Make dismissal a single action, not multi-step
Don't penalize or obstruct users who dismiss AI help
Offer 'don't show this again' options
Respect dismissal across sessions
Allow granular control over what AI features to disable

common_issues.issue: No way to dismiss AI outputs
common_issues.example: AI recommendations block interface with no close button
common_issues.impact: Users feel trapped and frustrated

common_issues.example: Dismissed suggestions reappear immediately or next session
common_issues.impact: Creates annoyance and trains users to ignore AI

common_issues.example: Dismissing requires multiple clicks or confirmation dialogs
common_issues.impact: Increases friction and user frustration

guidelines.description: Enable users to easily correct AI mistakes or provide feedback when outputs are wrong. Make the correction process quick and straightforward.
guidelines.intent: Allows users to fix errors and helps the AI learn. Easy correction improves both immediate user experience and long-term AI performance.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially learning systems and those prone to errors

questions: Can users easily correct AI mistakes?
Is correction a simple, low-effort process?
Does the AI learn from corrections?
Are correction options discoverable?
Can users provide feedback on AI outputs?

best_practices: Enable inline editing of AI outputs
Provide thumbs up/down or rating buttons
Allow users to report incorrect results
Make corrections single actions where possible
Show that corrections are being used to improve the AI
Support different types of feedback (wrong, inappropriate, irrelevant)
Learn from corrections to improve future outputs
Make correction options visible and accessible
Thank users for corrections to encourage feedback

common_issues.example: AI outputs text that can't be edited or corrected
common_issues.impact: Users must abandon AI output and start over manually

common_issues.example: Users report errors but AI keeps making same mistakes
common_issues.impact: Users lose trust and stop providing feedback

common_issues.example: Correcting requires navigating to separate feedback form
common_issues.impact: Users don't bother correcting, reducing AI learning

guidelines.interaction_phase: When the AI fails or is uncertain
guidelines.description: When the AI is uncertain or lacks confidence, it should narrow its scope or defer to the user rather than guessing broadly. Limit outputs to what the AI is confident about.
guidelines.intent: Prevents AI from making overconfident mistakes. Users prefer honest uncertainty to confident incorrectness.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially predictive and generative systems

questions: Does the AI narrow scope when uncertain?
Are low-confidence outputs flagged or withheld?
Does the AI defer to users in ambiguous situations?
Are conservative approaches used when stakes are high?
Does the AI avoid guessing when it doesn't know?
what_to_look_for: Narrowed suggestions rather than broad guesses

best_practices: Set confidence thresholds below which AI doesn't make suggestions
Offer narrower, more conservative options when uncertain
Explicitly state when the AI is uncertain
Ask clarifying questions rather than guessing
Provide multiple options with uncertainty rather than single guess
Escalate to human assistance when confidence is low
Use conservative defaults in high-stakes situations
Show confidence scores to help users judge outputs
Err on the side of caution rather than boldness

common_issues.example: Medical AI gives definitive diagnosis with low confidence data
common_issues.impact: Users may act on incorrect information with serious consequences

common_issues.issue: Guessing instead of asking for clarification
common_issues.example: AI makes assumptions about ambiguous queries instead of asking
common_issues.impact: Users receive irrelevant or wrong results

common_issues.example: All AI outputs presented with equal confidence regardless of certainty
common_issues.impact: Users cannot distinguish reliable from unreliable outputs

guidelines.guideline_name: Make clear why the system did what it did
guidelines.interaction_phase: When the AI fails or is uncertain
guidelines.description: Provide explanations for AI decisions and actions. Help users understand the reasoning behind AI outputs, especially when they are unexpected.
guidelines.intent: Builds understanding and appropriate trust. Users can better evaluate AI outputs and learn when to rely on the system when they understand its reasoning.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, critical for high-stakes and complex AI decisions

questions: Does the AI explain its decisions?
Are explanations understandable to users?
Can users see what factors influenced AI outputs?
Are explanations provided especially for unexpected results?
Is transparency balanced with usability?
what_to_look_for: Factors or features that influenced output
Different explanation depths for different users

best_practices: Provide 'Why this recommendation?' explanations
Show key factors that influenced the AI's decision
Use plain language, avoid technical jargon
Offer progressive disclosure (brief explanation with option for more detail)
Explain unexpected or surprising results
Show what data or inputs the AI used
Provide causal explanations when possible
Use visualizations to aid understanding
Tailor explanation complexity to user expertise
Make explanations optional to avoid clutter

common_issues.example: AI rejects loan application with no explanation of why
common_issues.impact: Users cannot understand or contest decisions, feel powerless

common_issues.example: Showing feature weights and model parameters to end users
common_issues.impact: Users cannot benefit from explanations they don't understand

common_issues.issue: Post-hoc rationalizations instead of true reasoning
common_issues.example: AI generates plausible-sounding but inaccurate explanations
common_issues.impact: Misleads users about how the AI actually works

guidelines.description: Maintain context and memory of recent user interactions. The AI should remember what just happened to provide coherent, contextual experiences.
guidelines.intent: Prevents frustrating repetition and creates more natural, efficient interactions. Users expect AI to remember recent context like a human conversation partner would.
guidelines.applicability: Conversational AI, assistants, multi-turn interactions, session-based systems

questions: Does the AI remember previous exchanges in the session?
Can users reference earlier parts of the conversation?
Is context maintained across related interactions?
Does the AI avoid asking for information already provided?
Is there appropriate session memory?

best_practices: Maintain conversation history throughout the session
Enable pronoun and reference resolution ('it', 'that', 'the previous one')
Don't ask for information the user just provided
Show conversation history so users can reference it
Persist context across related tasks in the same session
Resume interrupted conversations where they left off
Allow users to clear or reset context when needed
Balance memory with privacy (clear sensitive data appropriately)
Maintain context for a reasonable time window

common_issues.example: Chatbot treats each message as independent, losing conversation flow
common_issues.impact: Users must repeat information, conversation feels robotic

common_issues.example: User says their name, then AI asks 'What's your name?' two turns later
common_issues.impact: Frustrates users and wastes time

common_issues.example: User says 'make it blue' but AI doesn't remember what 'it' refers to
common_issues.impact: Forces unnatural, repetitive interactions

guidelines.description: Adapt and improve based on user behavior and patterns over time. The AI should personalize and become more helpful as it learns user preferences.
guidelines.intent: Creates increasingly valuable and personalized experiences. AI that learns becomes more efficient and aligned with individual user needs.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems with repeated user interactions, personalization engines

questions: Does the AI adapt to user preferences over time?
Are personalization improvements noticeable?
Does the system learn from user choices and corrections?
Is learning balanced with privacy concerns?
Can users see and control what the AI has learned?
what_to_look_for: Learning from user selections and rejections
User control over learning and personalization

best_practices: Learn from user selections, corrections, and dismissals
Personalize suggestions based on usage patterns
Adapt to user's communication style and preferences
Improve accuracy based on user feedback
Balance personalization with privacy (transparent data use)
Allow users to see and control learned preferences
Provide option to reset or modify learned profile
Start with reasonable defaults, improve through use
Show users how the AI is adapting ('Because you often...')
Learn incrementally without dramatic, jarring changes

common_issues.example: AI gives same generic results to every user regardless of history
common_issues.impact: Missed opportunity for improved relevance and efficiency

common_issues.example: AI only shows content similar to past choices, limiting discovery
common_issues.impact: Users miss diverse options and become trapped in narrow patterns

common_issues.example: AI changes behavior based on learning but users can't see or control it
common_issues.impact: Users feel loss of control and may not trust the system

guidelines.description: When updating AI behavior or models, do so gradually and carefully. Avoid sudden, dramatic changes that could confuse or frustrate users.
guidelines.intent: Maintains user trust and prevents disruption. Abrupt AI changes can break user workflows and expectations built over time.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems that update or retrain models, especially production systems

questions: Are AI updates gradual rather than sudden?
Do users receive notice of significant changes?
Are updates tested before wide deployment?
Can users provide feedback on updates?
Is there rollback capability if updates cause problems?

best_practices: Use gradual rollouts (A/B testing, phased deployment)
Notify users of significant AI behavior changes
Test updates thoroughly before deployment
Maintain backward compatibility when possible
Provide option to use previous version temporarily
Monitor user feedback and metrics after updates
Have rollback plans for problematic updates
Update incrementally rather than drastically
Preserve core functionality users rely on
Communicate the benefits of updates to users

common_issues.example: AI assistant completely changes personality overnight after update
common_issues.impact: Breaks user expectations and workflows, reduces trust

common_issues.example: Search algorithm changes significantly without informing users
common_issues.impact: Users confused by different results for same queries

common_issues.example: Model update deployed to all users immediately, causes widespread errors
common_issues.impact: Disrupts all users simultaneously, difficult to diagnose

guidelines.description: Solicit specific, detailed feedback from users rather than just binary ratings. Enable users to explain what was good or bad about AI outputs.
guidelines.intent: Provides richer signals for improvement. Specific feedback helps developers and AI systems understand what to fix and what to preserve.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially those that learn from feedback

questions: Can users provide detailed feedback beyond thumbs up/down?
Are there options to explain what was wrong?
Can users specify types of issues (irrelevant, biased, incorrect)?
Is granular feedback easy to provide?
Does the system act on specific feedback?

best_practices: Offer multiple feedback dimensions (accuracy, relevance, tone, etc.)
Provide categorized issue types (wrong, offensive, irrelevant, etc.)
Enable free-text explanations for feedback
Ask clarifying follow-up questions to simple ratings
Make feedback optional but easy to provide
Show users how their feedback improves the system
Use progressive disclosure (start simple, allow detailed feedback)
Allow feedback on specific parts of outputs, not just overall
Act on feedback and communicate improvements
Balance feedback requests with not being annoying

common_issues.example: Just thumbs up/down with no way to explain why
common_issues.impact: Cannot learn what specifically to improve

common_issues.example: Users report issues but never see improvements
common_issues.impact: Users stop providing feedback, feeling it's ignored

common_issues.example: Providing feedback requires filling out long surveys
common_issues.impact: Users don't bother, reducing feedback volume

guidelines.guideline_name: Convey the consequences of user actions
guidelines.description: Clearly communicate what will happen as a result of user actions, especially actions that affect AI behavior or learning. Users should understand the impact of their choices.
guidelines.intent: Enables informed decision-making. Users need to understand how their actions affect AI behavior to make good choices and maintain control.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially learning systems and those with persistent effects

questions: Are consequences of actions explained before users take them?
Do users understand how their actions affect AI behavior?
Are long-term effects communicated?
Is there preview of outcomes?
Are irreversible actions clearly marked?
what_to_look_for: Clear indication of reversible vs. irreversible actions
Examples of how choices affect AI

best_practices: Explain how feedback and corrections affect future AI behavior
Show previews or examples of consequences before users commit
Warn users about irreversible actions
Clarify which settings are immediate vs. learned over time
Use 'This will...' language to be explicit about effects
Show examples of how similar actions affected AI in the past
Communicate privacy implications of choices
Allow users to preview AI changes before applying them
Make consequences immediate and visible when possible

common_issues.example: Dismissing suggestion affects future recommendations but this isn't explained
common_issues.impact: Users unknowingly shape AI behavior in unintended ways

common_issues.example: Changing settings immediately affects AI with no way to see impact first
common_issues.impact: Users afraid to experiment with settings

common_issues.example: User doesn't know if action has temporary or permanent effect on AI
common_issues.impact: Users hesitant to interact, fearing unintended lasting changes

guidelines.description: Give users high-level controls over AI behavior and settings. Allow users to set overall preferences and boundaries for how AI operates.
guidelines.intent: Provides user agency and control. Users should be able to govern AI behavior at a system level, not just react to individual instances.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems, especially those with ongoing interactions

questions: Can users access system-wide AI settings?
Are there controls for overall AI behavior?
Can users set boundaries and preferences globally?
Are privacy controls available?
Can users disable or limit AI features?

best_practices: Provide centralized AI settings/preferences page
Allow users to disable AI features entirely
Offer controls for proactivity levels (how often AI suggests)
Enable privacy controls (data collection, personalization)
Allow users to reset AI learning and start fresh
Provide transparency controls (explanation detail levels)
Offer notification frequency settings
Allow export of user data and AI-learned preferences
Make controls discoverable and well-organized
Provide sensible defaults that work for most users

common_issues.example: AI settings scattered across interface with no global access
common_issues.impact: Users cannot manage overall AI behavior effectively

common_issues.example: AI assistance is forced with no opt-out option
common_issues.impact: Users feel lack of control, may abandon entire product

common_issues.issue: No privacy controls for AI learning
common_issues.example: AI learns from behavior with no way to limit or control data use
common_issues.impact: Privacy concerns may prevent users from engaging with AI

guidelines.description: Inform users when the AI system changes in significant ways, whether through updates, learning, or new capabilities. Keep users aware of evolution.
guidelines.intent: Maintains transparency and trust. Users should understand how and when AI systems change to calibrate expectations and trust appropriately.
guidelines.applicability: All AI systems that update or adapt over time

questions: Are users notified of significant AI updates?
Do users know when AI has learned new capabilities?
Are behavior changes communicated?
Is there changelog or update information?
Can users review recent changes?

best_practices: Notify users of significant AI capability additions
Communicate behavior changes that affect user experience
Provide changelogs for AI updates
Highlight new features with in-app announcements
Explain improvements in user-benefit terms
Time notifications appropriately (not disruptive)
Allow users to explore changes at their own pace
Provide 'What's new' summaries
Notify about both additions and removals
Balance transparency with not overwhelming users

common_issues.example: AI behavior changes but users aren't informed
common_issues.impact: Users confused by unexpected different behavior

common_issues.example: Release notes say 'model retrained' without explaining impact
common_issues.impact: Users cannot understand what actually changed

common_issues.issue: No way to review past changes
common_issues.example: No changelog or history of AI updates available
common_issues.impact: Users cannot trace when behavior changed or report issues

how_to_conduct_evaluation: 1. Identify the AI system's interaction phases (initially, during, when wrong, over time)
2. Select relevant guidelines based on system type and capabilities
3. For each applicable guideline, review evaluation criteria and questions
4. Document specific compliance or violations with examples
5. Assess severity of violations (critical, high, medium, low)
6. Prioritize issues based on severity and user impact
7. Review best practices for remediation guidance
8. Create action plan with specific improvements

initially.description: Guidelines that apply before users begin interacting with the AI

during.description: Guidelines that apply during normal AI operation

when_wrong.description: Guidelines for handling AI failures and uncertainty

over_time.description: Guidelines for AI systems that adapt and evolve
over_time.focus: Learning, adaptation, and long-term user relationships

severity_assessment.critical: Violates user safety, privacy, fairness, or causes significant harm
severity_assessment.high: Severely impacts usability, trust, or creates major frustration
severity_assessment.medium: Noticeably affects user experience or efficiency
severity_assessment.low: Minor inconvenience or missed opportunity for improvement

reporting_best_practices: Reference specific guideline number and name in findings
Include concrete examples with context (screenshots, scenarios)
Assess severity using the severity framework
Suggest specific remediation from best practices
Prioritize fixes based on severity and implementation effort
Consider guideline interactions (fixing one may affect others)
Re-test after fixes to verify compliance
